aiOverview.content: As of April 2026, the USPS is temporarily suspending contributions to its employee pension plans (FERS) to manage a "pending liquidity crisis," affecting roughly $400 million in monthly payments. USPS employees primarily participate in the Federal Employees Retirement System (FERS), which includes a defined benefit pension, Social Security, and the Thrift Savings Plan (TSP).Key components of the USPS retirement system include:FERS (Federal Employees Retirement System): This is the primary plan for most employees hired after 1984, combining a basic pension, Social Security, and the Thrift Savings Plan (TSP).CSRS (Civil Service Retirement System): A older system covering employees hired before 1984.Thrift Savings Plan (TSP): A defined contribution plan similar to a 401(k), with USPS matching contributions up to 5% of pay.Pension Calculation: Pension benefits are calculated based on years of service and the average of the highest three consecutive years of salary ("high-3").Recent Changes: Due to financial constraints, USPS announced in April 2026 that it is pausing employer payments to the pension fund to conserve cash.For official information on benefits, the USPS Compensation and Benefits page provides comprehensive details for employees.
